skill.name: join-meeting
skill.description: Join Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams as an AI meeting participant using AgentCall. The skill supports voice, transcripts, avatars, screenshare, chat, screenshots, and local webpage sharing.
skill.summary: Connect an AI agent to live meetings with voice, transcripts, avatars, and screenshare.
skill.author: pattern-ai-labs

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally connects a local AI agent to live meetings through AgentCall, including transcripts, voice, screenshots, screenshare, chat, and tunnels. Many static hits are false positives from Markdown fences or JavaScript template literals, but confirmed risks remain for credential handling, external transport, local filesystem access, screen capture, XSS-prone UI rendering, and transcript-driven agent control. It should not be auto-published without explicit consent flows, restricted permissions, and stronger data handling guidance.

remediation.issue: Meeting participants can influence a powerful agent through transcript input.
remediation.suggestion: Require permission allowlists, plan mode, or explicit confirmation before file edits, shell commands, commits, deployments, or external data access during calls.

remediation.issue: Meeting media and transcripts can leave the local machine.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear consent prompts and data handling disclosures before enabling transcripts, screenshots, capture, audio streaming, chat logging, or screenshare.

remediation.issue: Localhost tunnel features can expose unintended services or files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict tunnel routing to explicit ports and directories, warn on port conflicts, and avoid sharing URLs until the selected content is verified.

remediation.issue: API keys are stored in a plaintext hidden config file.
remediation.suggestion: Set restrictive file permissions, support OS keychain storage, and document how to rotate and delete AgentCall keys.

remediation.issue: Template UIs assign unescaped participant and transcript content with innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Render participant names, transcript text, and slide state with textContent or a sanitizer instead of raw innerHTML.
Remove eval guidance and recommend safe parsers or constrained calculation libraries for user-controlled expressions.

semantic_findings.title: Meeting Participants Can Steer a Full Agent Session
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that meeting transcripts arrive as agent input and that any participant can steer the agent. The README also says the agent keeps full session context and can search code, edit files, run commands, and commit changes while in the meeting.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly describe transcript-driven control and full agent capabilities. This creates a strong prompt-injection and authorization risk in meetings with untrusted participants.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Meeting Media Can Be Captured and Transferred
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports transcripts, screenshots, screen capture, chat, audio, avatars, and screenshare. These features can expose confidential meeting content through AgentCall services and local output files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited documentation explicitly lists talk, listen, screenshots, chat, and capture commands. The privacy risk follows directly from those supported capabilities.

semantic_findings.title: Localhost Tunnel Can Expose Local Web Content
semantic_findings.description: The skill lets the agent serve local webpages and share public tunnel URLs with meeting participants. If the wrong port or directory is selected, local services or generated files may become reachable through the tunnel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow and tunnel code show public URLs proxying requests to localhost ports. This is intended functionality but creates a clear exposure boundary.

content.user_title: Join Meetings With an AI Agent
content.value_statement: AI agents cannot attend live meetings without custom audio, video, and transcript plumbing. This skill connects them to Google Meet, Zoom, and Teams through AgentCall.
actual_capabilities: Join Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams as a bot participant.
Receive real-time transcripts, participant events, and meeting lifecycle events.
Speak in meetings with text-to-speech or webpage audio modes.
Show avatars, screenshares, dashboards, and local webpages through AgentCall tunnels.
Send and receive meeting chat messages, screenshots, and capture frames.
Save AgentCall API keys and default meeting preferences in a local config file.
limitations: Requires an AgentCall account, API key, credits, and network access.
Sends meeting audio, transcripts, screenshots, and tunnel data through AgentCall services.
Requires local Python or Node dependencies and a subprocess-capable agent framework.
Meeting participants can influence the agent through transcripts unless permissions are restricted.

use_cases.title: Pair Programming Call
use_cases.description: Let a coding agent discuss code, answer questions, and share progress during a live engineering meeting.

use_cases.title: Support or Demo Assistant
use_cases.description: Join a customer call with a voice assistant that can answer questions and share visual materials.

use_cases.title: Meeting Notes and Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Use passive mode to collect transcripts, summarize decisions, and prepare action items after the call.

prompt_templates.title: Join a Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Join this meeting as a helpful voice participant: <meeting link>. Use audio mode and introduce yourself when someone joins.

prompt_templates.title: Take Silent Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Join this meeting as a silent note taker: <meeting link>. Do not speak. Summarize decisions and action items after it ends.

prompt_templates.title: Join With Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Join this meeting with an avatar and collaborative voice: <meeting link>. Use the default visual template and respond when addressed.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Guarded Working Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Join this meeting for a coding session: <meeting link>. Use restricted tool permissions, confirm before file edits, and share progress visually.

output_examples.input: Join this Google Meet as Juno and help answer product questions.
output: The bot joins the meeting and waits for a participant.
It introduces itself by voice, listens to transcript events, and answers when addressed.
After the call ends, it provides a short summary and cleanup status.

output_examples.input: Join as a silent note taker and do not speak.
output: The bot joins without speaking and collects transcript events.
The final response lists decisions, open questions, owners, and action items.

output_examples.input: Join with screenshare and show the dashboard when I ask.
output: The bot starts with voice and avatar only.
When requested, it shares the prepared dashboard and narrates the key points.

best_practices: Use trusted meetings and restrict agent permissions before joining calls.
Tell participants when the bot records transcripts, screenshots, audio, or screenshare content.
End calls cleanly and remove temporary files that contain meeting content.
anti_patterns: Do not join untrusted calls with file write, shell, or deployment permissions enabled.
Do not expose arbitrary localhost ports through the tunnel.
Do not use screenshots or recording features without participant consent.

faq.question: Which meeting platforms does this support?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams through AgentCall.

faq.question: Does it require an AgentCall API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts read an AgentCall API key from an environment variable or local config file.

faq.question: Can the bot speak during the meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use direct text-to-speech or collaborative voice intelligence for group conversations.

faq.question: Can it run inside Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, plus other subprocess-capable agents.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: Meeting URLs, transcripts, audio, screenshots, tunnel traffic, and control events can pass through AgentCall services.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential meetings?
faq.answer: Only with explicit consent, trusted participants, restricted agent permissions, and clear data handling controls.
